title: A Finite Boole Summation Formula for Alternating Sums
description: When an alternating series ∑ (-1)^j a_j is truncated, the remainder is to leading order half the first omitted term, with an asymptotic correction series in the discrete derivatives of a (the Boole / Euler–Maclaurin expansion R_n ~ ((-1)^n/2)[a_n − (1/4)a_n'' + ⋯]). The rigorous engine behind this heuristic is an exact finite identity needing no convergence: writing Δa_j = a_{j+1} − a_j and altSum a n m = ∑_{j=n}^{m-1} (-1)^j a_j, the first-order Boole summation formula reads altSum a n m = ½·((-1)^n a_n − (-1)^m a_m) − ½·altSum (Δa) n m. The leading endpoint term ½·(-1)^n a_n is exactly half the first term; the residual is the same alternating sum applied to the forward differences, one order smaller. This entry proves the first- and second-order formulas (the latter exposing the Δ²a correction matching the a'' term), an exact error identity, a total-variation remainder bound |altSum − model| ≤ ½∑|Δa_j|, and for a decreasing sequence the telescoped bound ½(a_n − a_m) — the precise finite form of 'remainder ≈ half the first omitted term'. All results are over ℝ, elementary, and axiom-free; Mathlib has the alternating series test but not this summation identity.

overview.historicalContext: Boole summation is the alternating-sign companion of the Euler–Maclaurin formula: where Euler–Maclaurin relates a sum ∑ f(j) to an integral plus a series in the Bernoulli numbers, Boole summation relates an alternating sum ∑ (-1)^j f(j) to boundary terms plus a series in the Euler numbers. The headline consequence, known to every student of the alternating series test, is that the truncation remainder is approximately half the first omitted term — far better than the crude 'error ≤ first term' from Leibniz alone. The exact statement is an operator identity ½/(1+E)·(boundary data) with E the shift; expanded it produces the discrete-derivative corrections a_n, a_n'', … of the asymptotic series.
overview.problemStatement:
Truncating an alternating series ∑ (-1)^j a_j leaves a remainder R_n. How is R_n related to the first omitted term, exactly and to higher order?

**Answer (finite, exact).** With altSum a n m = ∑_{j=n}^{m-1} (-1)^j a_j and Δa_j = a_{j+1} − a_j,

altSum a n m = ½·((-1)^n a_n − (-1)^m a_m) − ½·altSum (Δa) n m.

The leading term ½·(-1)^n a_n is half the first term; the residual is an alternating sum of differences, one order smaller. Iterating gives the Δ²a correction; the difference from the half-endpoint model is bounded by ½∑|Δa_j|, which for a decreasing a telescopes to ½(a_n − a_m).
overview.text: An exact, axiom-free finite identity expressing an alternating sum as half its endpoint terms plus a smaller alternating sum of the forward differences — the rigorous engine behind 'the remainder is half the first omitted term'.
keyInsights: Boole summation is exact and finite: no convergence is needed — the asymptotic 'remainder ≈ half first term' is a corollary of an algebraic identity that holds for every window [n, m)
The identity is discrete summation by parts: pairing (-1)^j against the antidifference of the sign sequence turns ∑(-1)^j a_j into endpoint terms minus ½∑(-1)^j Δa_j
Each iteration lowers the order: the residual is the same operation applied to Δa, so one step yields the Δ²a (≈ a'') correction with coefficient 1/4 — the start of the Euler-number expansion
The half-endpoint model has a clean error control: |altSum − model| ≤ ½ total-variation(a), telescoping to ½(a_n − a_m) for monotone a, which → ½ a_n as the upper terms vanish

The iteration closes to a single order-K identity (boole_general): ∑_{k<K} ((-1)^k/2^{k+1})·endpoint(Δᵏa) plus an exact alternating-sum remainder of Δᴷa, proved by induction on K and recovering boole_first/boole_second at K=1,2
prerequisites: Finite sums over half-open integer intervals Finset.Ico and Finset.sum_Ico_succ_top
Forward differences and discrete summation by parts (Abel summation)
Triangle inequality for finite sums; telescoping of monotone differences
overview.proofStrategy: Define altSum over Finset.Ico n m and the forward difference fdiff. Prove the one-step recurrence altSum_succ from Finset.sum_Ico_succ_top. For boole_first, induct on m ≥ n with Nat.le_induction: the base case m = n is the empty sum, and the successor step rewrites both alternating sums via altSum_succ, substitutes the inductive hypothesis and fdiff, and closes by ring (the sign flip (-1)^{m+1} = −(-1)^m is handled by pow_succ). boole_second follows by applying boole_first to the differences and simplifying by ring. The error identity altSum_sub_half_endpoints is a one-line rearrangement of boole_first; the total-variation bound altSum_sub_half_endpoints_abs_le combines it with abs_altSum_le (triangle inequality, using |(-1)^j| = 1). For antitone a, sum_abs_fdiff_antitone telescopes ∑|Δa_j| = a_n − a_m by induction, giving the half-first-term estimate altSum_sub_half_first_le_antitone.

sections.title: Header: A finite Boole summation formula for alternating sums
sections.summary: Motivates the exact finite identity behind the heuristic 'truncation remainder is half the first omitted term': a first-order formula expressing a truncated alternating sum via its endpoints minus a residual alternating sum of forward differences, iterated to arbitrary order $K$ with explicit error bounds and an exactness result on polynomial sequences.

sections.title: Alternating Sum and Forward Difference

sections.title: First-Order Boole Summation Formula

sections.summary: Iterating once on the differences yields the second-difference term with coefficient 1/4, the discrete analogue of the a'' correction.

sections.summary: altSum − model = −½·altSum(Δa); hence |altSum − model| ≤ ½∑|Δa_j| via the triangle inequality (|(-1)^j| = 1).

sections.title: Half-First-Term Estimate for Decreasing Sequences
sections.summary: For antitone a the total variation telescopes to a_n − a_m, giving |altSum − model| ≤ ½(a_n − a_m) — the finite form of 'remainder ≈ half the first omitted term'.

sections.title: Higher-Order Monotone Telescoping
sections.summary: sum_abs_fdiff_monotone / sum_abs_fdiff_of_monotone_or_antitone telescope the total variation of a monotone sequence to |a_m − a_n| (either direction). Feeding this into the order-(K+1) remainder bound gives altSum_sub_booleModel_le_of_iterate_monotone: when the K-th difference Δᴷa is monotone the error collapses to (1/2^{K+1})·|(Δᴷa)_m − (Δᴷa)_n|, the exact 'remainder ≈ leading Boole term' statement at every order.
sections.mathContext: $\big|\mathrm{altSum} - \text{model}_{K+1}\big| \le \tfrac{1}{2^{K+1}}\,\big|(\Delta^K a)_m - (\Delta^K a)_n\big|$ when $\Delta^K a$ is monotone; $K=0$ recovers the antitone half-first-term estimate, $K=1$ (convex decreasing $a$) gives $\tfrac14|\Delta a_m - \Delta a_n|$.

sections.title: Exactness on Polynomial Sequences and Closed Forms
sections.summary: When Δᴷa ≡ 0 the order-K Boole remainder vanishes (boole_exact_of_iterate_fdiff_zero), so the alternating sum equals its finite Boole endpoint model with no residual; instantiated for affine sequences (altSum_affine: Δ²(α+βj)=0 gives an exact pure-endpoint closed form) and constants (altSum_const).

conclusion.summary: The "remainder ≈ half the first omitted term" heuristic for alternating series is grounded in an exact, axiom-free finite identity: altSum a n m = ½·((-1)^n a_n − (-1)^m a_m) − ½·altSum (Δa) n m. Iterating it to all orders gives the general order-K Boole formula boole_general — the first K weights (-1)^k/2^{k+1} times the endpoint differences of Δᵏa, plus an exact remainder that is an alternating sum of Δᴷa — with a matching error bound (1/2^K)·∑|Δᴷa_j|. For a decreasing sequence the K=1 case telescopes to ½(a_n − a_m).
conclusion.implications: Provides the reusable Boole summation engine — discrete summation by parts specialised to the alternating sign — that Mathlib does not package, complementing its alternating series test. The finite identity yields the leading half-term estimate without any convergence hypothesis, and boole_general gives the full finite Euler-number expansion to arbitrary order K as a single closed form with an explicit (1/2^K)-shrinking remainder bound.
openQuestions: Does taking m → ∞ for a convergent alternating series (a → 0) give a clean tsum-level statement R_n = ½(-1)^n a_n − ½·(tail alternating sum of Δa), tying the finite engine to Mathlib’s limit?
Do the Boole weights (-1)^k/2^{k+1} of boole_general match the Euler numbers / Euler polynomials evaluated at a fixed point, and can that be proved as an exact rational identity within the gallery?

crossReferences.description: The alternating series test bounds the remainder by the whole first omitted term (|S_N − l| ≤ a_N); Boole summation refines this to half that term plus a smaller difference sum.
